notes:
I couldn't do any of the research, so I haven't written any notes.

My first attempt to open the sources (Enduring Word, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Gill on Bible Hub, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes) was blocked with the message "no more code_execution tool calls remaining this turn." A second try was blocked the same way. Since no page was read, I have nothing I can tie to a URL. Your rules say to report only what the pages say, so I haven't filled any of it in from memory.

If you send the request again in a new message, the limit should reset and I'll start with these:

- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** enduringword.com (Hosea 6); biblehub.com (Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Gill on Hosea 6); preceptaustin.org (Hosea 6).
- **Protestant differences:** the main place I'd look is v. 7 ("like Adam"). I'd check Reformed sources (ligonier.org, monergism.com) against Wesleyan and Baptist ones. I'd also look at how teachers on each side read v. 2 ("on the third day") and v. 6 ("mercy, not sacrifice").
- **Other views:** netbible.org notes on the hard wording in vv. 2, 7 and 11; newadvent.org for early Church writers on vv. 2 and 6; bibleodyssey.org for modern scholarship; gotquestions.org on how popular teaching uses v. 6.

If you'd rather get fewer, more reliable notes, I could also start with just one or two sources, such as Enduring Word and Bible Hub.
